title: Credit Economics: Stop Streaming Static Catalog Feeds

steps.prompt: Data 360 credits are burning down early each month. An audit finds 50 streaming connectors on product catalog tables that change about once a week, while scarce credit headroom is needed for real-time behavioral streams. What refactor is required?

options.label: Transition slow-changing catalog data streams from continuous streaming to daily batch ingestion
options.rationale: Streaming connectors consume continuous compute credits for micro-batch polling; switching weekly/daily reference data to scheduled batch drastically reduces credit burn.

options.label: Increase the streaming buffer flush interval to 60 minutes while keeping continuous connectors
options.distractorAntipattern: Adjusting flush intervals does not eliminate the fixed infrastructure credit cost of 50 active streaming listener connections.
options.rationale: Increasing flush intervals reduces message write frequency but still maintains 50 continuous streaming compute workers, yielding minimal credit savings.

options.label: Consolidate all 50 product catalog tables into a single high-frequency Ingestion API endpoint
options.distractorAntipattern: Directing 50 tables through a continuous Ingestion API endpoint still incurs streaming ingestion credit tariffs.
options.rationale: Streaming static reference data via the Ingestion API still bills at continuous streaming rates rather than lower-cost batch processing tiers.
